chapters.screenText: Initialize native ISSM from your gridded MATLAB fields.
chapters.screenWhy: Full geometry and velocity fields must initialize the actual native mesh.
chapters.expectedResult: Four scripts + issm-shelf-initial.mat; verified BYO AWS, MATLAB and Connector.
chapters.title: 1. Prepare your files and access
instructions: Open Pilot Tutorials → Upload a dataset → download the native initial-condition packet. Extract it.
Have an approved login, connected AWS resources and configured MATLAB/Connector. Choose Cloud → Advanced → ISSM.
chapters.why: Full geometry and velocity fields must initialize the actual native mesh.
chapters.note: Scripts: native-data-issm-mat/ (all four files). Data: datasets/issm-shelf-initial.mat. Prerequisites are linked on the tutorial page.

chapters.screenText: Name an owned example, then choose New example.
chapters.screenWhy: An owned example keeps your imported workflow separate from installed examples.
chapters.expectedResult: Expected: a new editable ISSM workspace example.
chapters.title: 2. Create an owned example
instructions: In Editor, enter a new name and choose New example.
This recording uses pilot-issm-mat-1119. A new ISSM example can include a seeded runme.m that must be replaced with your real script.
chapters.why: An owned example keeps your imported workflow separate from installed examples.
chapters.note: A seeded runme.m must be replaced by the supplied MAT run script before launch.

chapters.screenText: Read the confirmation and keep this owned example selected.
chapters.screenWhy: Source imports and dataset attachments must belong to the same example.
chapters.expectedResult: Expected: the newly created workspace name.
chapters.title: 2. Confirm the owned workspace
instructions: The blue confirmation says the workspace example was created.
Keep this owned example selected while uploading and referencing the input. Source files and datasets use different controls.
chapters.why: Source imports and dataset attachments must belong to the same example.
chapters.note: This is an editable workspace example, separate from the read-only application examples.

chapters.screenWhy: The MAT file contains the full synthetic initial-condition grids.
chapters.expectedResult: Expected: one selected file becomes Uploaded: issm-shelf-initial.mat.
chapters.title: 3. Upload the MAT file
instructions: Scroll below Environment & resources in the left column to Datasets. Choose issm-shelf-initial.mat, then choose Upload. The selected-file count changes from 1 to 0 after upload.
This is a synthetic 5×9 gridded field file for a 10 km square shelf.
chapters.why: The MAT file contains the full synthetic initial-condition grids.
chapters.note: Upload stores the file. The script and schema-specific reader must still load it.

chapters.screenText: Select the MAT dataset and choose Reference in example.
chapters.screenWhy: Referencing provides the exact relative path that runme.m reads.
chapters.expectedResult: Expected: data/issm-shelf-initial.mat; do not add data/ twice.
chapters.title: 4. Reference the staged filename
instructions: Select issm-shelf-initial.mat and choose Reference in example. Keep the baseline filename.
The confirmation gives data/issm-shelf-initial.mat. The run script must read that exact relative path.
chapters.why: Referencing provides the exact relative path that runme.m reads.
chapters.note: Do not add data/ twice. Referencing makes the bytes available; it does not start the model.

chapters.screenText: Replace and import all four source files.
chapters.screenWhy: Replacement updates the new example’s starter runme.m.
chapters.expectedResult: Check count 4 → 0 and wait for Files are saved.
chapters.title: 5. Import all four source files
instructions: Choose runme.m, Launch.par, validate_launch_dataset.m and load_initial_conditions.m together.
Check Replace existing script files for the seeded runme.m, then choose Import script files.
chapters.why: Replacement updates the new example’s starter runme.m.
chapters.note: The actual continuous take shows selected count 4, replacement enabled, the import action and then count 0.

chapters.screenText: Confirm all four imported filenames and Files are saved.
chapters.screenWhy: Only saved scripts enter the next run snapshot.
chapters.title: 6. Check the saved-file confirmation
instructions: The confirmation names all four imported files and says Files are saved.
The imported runme.m is now the actual MAT reader/ISSM workflow. All four script hashes were verified before launch and in the submitted snapshot.
chapters.why: Only saved scripts enter the next run snapshot.
chapters.note: All four filenames must appear in the saved-file confirmation before you continue.

chapters.screenText: Confirm Action Run and Run target runme.m.
chapters.screenWhy: The entrypoint chooses the MATLAB workflow that will execute.
chapters.expectedResult: Keep all four saved scripts and the referenced MAT file.
chapters.title: 6. Confirm the entry script
instructions: In Experiment, confirm Action = Run and Run target = runme.m.
Importing source files does not select a different target or submit an AWS job.
chapters.why: The entrypoint chooses the MATLAB workflow that will execute.
chapters.note: The four saved scripts and the referenced MAT file must all be present before review.

chapters.screenText: Review the owned MAT experiment before launching.
chapters.screenWhy: Review checks resources, readiness, configured license and Connector.
chapters.title: 7. Review the MAT experiment
instructions: Choose Review & Launch. Confirm model ISSM and example pilot-issm-mat-1119, readiness and resources.
Scroll to the bottom of the review and choose Launch cloud run explicitly.
chapters.why: Review checks resources, readiness, configured license and Connector.
chapters.note: Check 2 vCPU / 8 GiB and the existing license/Connector. Measured execution times appear in the completion card.

chapters.screenText: Launch explicitly, then follow the new MAT run.
chapters.screenWhy: The new submission is the run to monitor through completion.
chapters.expectedResult: Expected: Staging/Submitting, then Queued, Running and Completed.
chapters.title: 7. Watch the new submission
instructions: Confirm Launch cloud run at the bottom of the review.
Watch the MAT experiment progress through Staging/Submitting, then wait for Queued, Running and Completed.
chapters.why: The new submission is the run to monitor through completion.
chapters.note: The manifest links the actual saved source/data, pinned image, job and retained archive.

chapters.screenWhy: The saved native figure shows the uploaded fields on the Triangle mesh.
chapters.expectedResult: Thickness 300–500 m; coordinates span a 10 km square.
chapters.title: 8a. Initial thickness
instructions: Initial thickness is 300–500 m.
The axes span a 10 km square in metres.
chapters.why: The saved native figure shows the uploaded fields on the Triangle mesh.
chapters.note: Exact saved native PNG, shown as the complete three-panel strip; this panel is outlined without stretching or altering pixels.

chapters.screenWhy: Floating-shelf base and surface must remain consistent with thickness.
chapters.expectedResult: Surface elevation and coordinates are in metres.
chapters.title: 8b. Initial surface
instructions: Surface elevation is in metres.
This floating shelf uses consistent thickness, base and surface.
chapters.why: Floating-shelf base and surface must remain consistent with thickness.
chapters.note: Exact saved native PNG, shown as the complete three-panel strip; this panel is outlined without stretching or altering pixels.

chapters.screenWhy: The diagnostic solver then computes the native velocity response.
chapters.expectedResult: Initial speed uses metres/year; this is not a transient time plot.
chapters.title: 8c. Initial speed
instructions: Initial speed is in metres/year.
The next diagnostic solve computes the native velocity field.
chapters.why: The diagnostic solver then computes the native velocity response.
chapters.note: Exact saved native PNG, shown as the complete three-panel strip; this panel is outlined without stretching or altering pixels.

chapters.screenText: Check all five initialized fields and successful completion.
chapters.screenWhy: A file upload is useful only when its fields actually initialize the model.
chapters.expectedResult: All five fields × 13 native vertices: interpolation error 0.
chapters.title: 9. Verify initialization and completion
instructions: Initialized thickness, base, surface, vx and vy match the uploaded file at all 13 native vertices, with maximum error 0.
One diagnostic SSA Stressbalance solve completed; no physical time advances.
chapters.why: A file upload is useful only when its fields actually initialize the model.
chapters.note: Startup 220.723 s · AWS task 51.018 s · script 9.568328 s, including setup, mesh, initial plotting and solving.

chapters.screenWhy: Render updates the retained native field without rerunning the model.
chapters.expectedResult: Expected: the accepted MAT run’s 13-node velocity field.
chapters.title: 10. Render the current velocity field
instructions: Open Workspace → Results for the completed MAT run. Confirm StressbalanceSolution and Vel, then choose Render.
The enabled button changes while the retained native velocity field is rendered.
chapters.why: Render updates the retained native field without rerunning the model.
chapters.note: This Results identity belongs to the accepted MAT run; the final native field contains 13 vertices and 16 triangles.

chapters.screenText: Inspect the saved final native velocity figure.
chapters.screenWhy: Use the full axes, colour bar and velocity components together.
chapters.expectedResult: Speed 100–180 m/year; Vel agrees with hypot(Vx,Vy).
chapters.title: 11. Inspect final native velocity
instructions: This is the unchanged native PNG from the accepted archive, with full axes and colour bar.
Speed is 100–180 m/year, and Vel agrees with hypot(Vx,Vy). The initial and solved velocities need not match in the interior.
chapters.why: Use the full axes, colour bar and velocity components together.
chapters.note: The mesh spans 10 km × 10 km. This diagnostic run has no transient time axis.

chapters.screenText: Use node-weighted definitions when reading these metrics.
chapters.screenWhy: Arithmetic-node metrics differ from area-weighted triangle metrics.
chapters.expectedResult: Mean h 402.307692 m; node-RMS speed 142.564238 m/year; iteration count 12.
chapters.title: 12. Interpret the checks precisely
instructions: Arithmetic-node mean thickness is 402.307692 m. Node-RMS speed sqrt(mean(Vel²)) is 142.564238 m/year; convergence count is the scalar 12.
These metrics are not area-weighted.
chapters.why: Arithmetic-node metrics differ from area-weighted triangle metrics.
chapters.note: Five inferred non-front boundary vertices match input vx/vy. Saved spc arrays remain opaque; this boundary check is an inference, not direct decoding.

chapters.screenText: Choose Download results and wait for the fresh link.
chapters.screenWhy: The archive preserves fields, figures, initialization and runtime provenance.
chapters.expectedResult: Expected: a newly prepared results_bundle link for this selected run.
chapters.title: 13. Prepare the archive download
instructions: Choose Download results. When the fresh HTTPS link appears, use it to save this run’s archive.
The next step follows that link; the archive contains the native fields, figures, initialized arrays and provenance.
chapters.why: The archive preserves fields, figures, initialization and runtime provenance.
chapters.note: Download preparation uses the completed run’s retained results.

chapters.screenText: Choose the fresh archive link to save this run’s results.
chapters.screenWhy: Keep the archive with its source, data, image and output hashes.
chapters.expectedResult: 15 CRC-valid members, byte-identical to the originally checked MAT archive.
chapters.title: 14. Save and check your archive
instructions: Click the fresh download link. The browser saved a 15-member ZIP with valid CRC.
Every file is byte-identical to the originally checked MAT archive. Keep the archive with its input, image and output hashes.
chapters.why: Keep the archive with its source, data, image and output hashes.
chapters.note: One native execution; this cached download does not rerun the solver. Repeatability and accuracy require separate checks.
